title.rendered: Peace I Leave With You: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.” A morning devotional on the peace that is not from the world and cannot be taken by the world.

content.rendered:
The world offers a peace it cannot deliver. A peace that lasts as long as the circumstances hold, then disappears the moment they don’t. Jesus offered a different peace, and He was specific about the difference.

The Gospel For Today | Wednesday, September 16, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.”
John 14:27 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

The world has a peace it markets constantly. It is the peace of the paid-off mortgage, the successful career, the healthy check-up, the child who has finally settled into a good school, the political leader who has finally been elected, the season of life when nothing seems to be going wrong. It is a real peace, in the sense that it does bring relief. It is also a fragile peace. It lasts exactly as long as the circumstances hold. A phone call, a diagnosis, a market shift, a betrayal, an accident, and the peace is gone in an afternoon. This is the peace the world gives. Jesus, in the upper room the night before the cross, was very specific that His peace was a different peace. “Peace I leave with you, My peace I give to you; not as the world gives do I give to you.”

Jesus’ peace does not depend on circumstances. It does not evaporate when the phone rings. It does not require a paid-off mortgage or a healthy check-up. It is anchored in something the world cannot touch, cannot take away, cannot replicate. It is the peace that comes from being loved by the Father, reconciled through the Son, sealed by the Spirit, and secure in an eternal destiny that no earthly loss can undo. It is the peace that allowed Paul and Silas to sing hymns in a Philippian jail with their feet in the stocks. It is the peace that allowed Stephen to pray for those stoning him. It is the peace that allowed Corrie ten Boom to forgive her sister’s Ravensbrück concentration camp guard. It is not a peace the circumstances produce. It is a peace the Prince of Peace produces, and gives, personally, to His followers.

The Passion Translation opens up the promise beautifully: “I leave the gift of peace with you—my peace. Not the kind of fragile peace given by the world, but my perfect peace. Don’t yield to fear or be troubled in your hearts—instead, be courageous!” (John 14:27 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “Peace I leave with you; My [own] peace I now give and bequeath to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Do not let your hearts be troubled, neither let them be afraid. [Stop allowing yourselves to be agitated and disturbed; and do not permit yourselves to be fearful and intimidated and cowardly and unsettled]” (John 14:27 AMPC). Stop allowing yourselves. The peace is available. Receiving it is a choice.

The Greek word for “peace” here is eirēnē, the New Testament equivalent of the Hebrew shalom. It does not mean the absence of trouble. It means the presence of wholeness. Everything as it should be, at the deepest level. A person can have eirēnē while circumstances are shaking, because eirēnē is not about the circumstances. It is about the anchor of the soul in the Father’s love. That is why Jesus was able to speak this promise on the night before the cross. He had less peaceful circumstances than most of us will ever face. And yet He was the source of the peace He was giving.

For Gospelbuzz readers today, this is the peace Jesus is offering. Wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, in the current season of your life, the world may be offering you its brittle version. Peace when the market is up. Peace when the diagnosis is good. Peace when the relationships are working. Jesus is offering the deeper thing. His peace. Anchored in Him. Available to you now, in whatever circumstances you are actually walking through. Receive it. Refuse to yield to fear. His peace guards the heart of every believer who will let it in.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Jesus has left me His peace, not the world’s peace. His peace does not depend on my circumstances. It is anchored in Your love for me, the finished work of Christ, and the seal of the Holy Spirit in my life. Today I refuse to yield to fear. I refuse to be intimidated by the news, the diagnosis, the bank balance, the uncertain future. His peace guards my heart and mind. I let it in. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

Jesus has left me His peace, not the world’s peace. My peace does not depend on my circumstances. It is anchored in the Father’s love, the finished work of Christ, and the Spirit’s seal on my life.
